newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai grains market quiet, feed mills buy corn.
newsitem.headline: Thai grains market quiet, feed mills buy corn.

text.p: Trade in the Thai grains and oilseed market was moderate over the week as players awaited a government decision on zero-tariff corn imports, traders said on Tuesday.

Even though the government had yet to approve the industry's request to import 150,000 tonnes of tariff-free corn, some major feed producers could not wait and had already imported out of the zero-tariff quota.
Chareon Pokphand was said to have bought 57,200 tonnes of Argentine corn. The vessel Anangel Argonaut was scheduled to arrive with the consignment at the end of the month.
Despite the high tariff rate, the company, which exports meat and poultry, can claim back the tariff under the government's scheme to waive tariffs on raw materials imported for export business.
The uncertain direction of the baht and the economy also put a lot of buyers on the sidelines, traders said.

"It's small-time end-users who were to be hit hardest. They don't know what kind of cost they are facing...whether the government will exercise certain controls over food prices," said a source from Thai Soymeal Trader and Importer Association, which imports mostly for end users.
"Soymeal demand for end users were covererd until September. They can afford to monitor the situation for some time," he said.
Soymeal prices were steady at 9.85 baht a kg ($0.32) while corn prices edged up slightly to 5.10-5.20 baht from 5.00-5.10 last week.
